pathway.title: Urinary Tract Infection and Asymptomatic Bacteriuria in Pregnancy — Outpatient Screening, Treatment and Surveillance
pathway.scope: US outpatient prenatal care. Universal early-pregnancy screening for asymptomatic bacteriuria; treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria and acute cystitis; the group B streptococcus bacteriuria arm; test of cure; recurrence and suppressive prophylaxis. Ends at the trigger for admission with pyelonephritis.
pathway.target_population: All pregnant patients receiving prenatal care. Screening applies universally; treatment and surveillance arms apply to those with a positive culture.

properties.title: Diabetes or spinal cord injury?
Urine culture at or above 100,000 CFU/mL?
Urine culture at or above 100,000 CFU/mL? (classify ASB vs cystitis)
Did the urine culture grow group B streptococcus?
properties.prompt: Did this urine culture grow group B streptococcus (Streptococcus agalactiae), at any colony count? A positive result at any count obliges intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis and removes the need for the 36 0/7-37 6/7 week rectovaginal screening culture.

properties.title: Fever, or acute pyelonephritis coded, with urine studies suggesting UTI?
Does the patient have urinary symptoms?
properties.prompt: Does the patient have urinary symptoms - new or worsening dysuria, haematuria, urinary frequency, or nocturia? Frequency, urgency and nocturia overlap with ordinary pregnancy symptoms; dysuria and haematuria carry the signal. Symptoms distinguish acute cystitis from asymptomatic bacteriuria, and test of cure is offered for cystitis only.

properties.title: Documented penicillin or beta-lactam allergy?
Documented penicillin or beta-lactam allergy? (clindamycin susceptibility request)
Is the patient in the first trimester?
properties.prompt: Is the patient in the first trimester (less than 14 0/7 weeks)? Nitrofurantoin and sulfonamides remain REASONABLE in the first trimester if no appropriate alternative is available - this is a preference, not a prohibition. Alternatives: cephalexin, fosfomycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate.

properties.title: Group B streptococcus at or above 100,000 CFU/mL, or symptomatic?
properties.prompt: Is the group B streptococcus colony count 100,000 CFU/mL or greater, OR is the patient symptomatic? Either warrants antepartum treatment. A lower count in an asymptomatic patient requires no antepartum antibiotic - but still obliges intrapartum prophylaxis.

properties.title: Has the antibiotic course been completed?
properties.prompt: Has the patient completed her antibiotic course? Follow-up, test of cure and recurrence assessment all key off completion, not off the prescription date.

properties.title: Two or more UTI episodes this pregnancy?

properties.name: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals 100 mg
properties.instructions: ACOG's closest thing to a preferred agent - low resistance, concentrates in the bladder. NOT for pyelonephritis: cannot reach therapeutic renal levels, and must be avoided when cystitis versus pyelonephritis is uncertain. Avoid in G6PD deficiency (haemolytic anaemia). Contraindicated at CrCl below 60 mL/min. FDA LABEL NOTE, retained for the prescriber and deliberately not gated per physician direction: label-contraindicated at 38-42 weeks, during labour, and when labour is imminent, because of neonatal haemolytic anaemia risk.

properties.name: Cephalexin 250-500 mg
properties.instructions: Appropriate for penicillin allergy at LOW anaphylaxis risk. Reaches therapeutic renal levels, unlike nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin.

properties.name: Fosfomycin 3 g
properties.instructions: The only single-dose option - ACOG calls it a reasonable choice for 1-day treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria. NOT for pyelonephritis, same renal-penetration limit as nitrofurantoin.

properties.name: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 800/160 mg
properties.instructions: Avoid empirically where local trimethoprim resistance exceeds 20%. First-trimester use is reasonable if no appropriate alternative is available. CROSS-PATHWAY CONTRAINDICATION: contraindicated in documented folate-deficiency megaloblastic anaemia and interferes with folate metabolism - conflicts with the anemia pathway's folate-repletion lane, and the lane mechanism cannot detect this.

properties.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 500/125 or 875/125 mg
properties.instructions: AVOID EMPIRICALLY - high E. coli resistance (39-48% to ampicillin). Reasonable once susceptibility is known.
properties.dose: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours

properties.name: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg, suppressive
properties.instructions: Per ACOG, suppression continues for the remainder of the pregnancy. FDA LABEL NOTE, retained for the prescriber and deliberately not gated per physician direction: label-contraindicated at 38-42 weeks, during labour, and when labour is imminent, because of neonatal haemolytic anaemia risk. Cephalexin is the label-safe alternative if a switch is preferred. Match to the isolate's susceptibility.

properties.name: Cephalexin 250-500 mg, suppressive
properties.instructions: Co-equal with nitrofurantoin for suppression. Match to the isolate's susceptibility. Continuous or postcoital dosing are both acceptable strategies.

properties.name: Clindamycin
properties.instructions: MUST NOT be used to treat group B streptococcus bacteriuria or any urinary tract infection, even in penicillin allergy - it concentrates poorly in urine and is metabolised primarily by the liver. A clindamycin susceptibility result on an antepartum GBS urine culture exists ONLY to guide intrapartum prophylaxis.

properties.topic: When to call us right away
properties.instructions: You are being treated for a bladder infection. Most people feel better within a day or two. But a bladder infection can move up to the kidneys, and a kidney infection in pregnancy is serious. Call right away - do not wait for your next appointment - if you get any of these: a fever of 100.4F (38C) or higher; pain in your back or your side, usually just below the ribs; shaking chills; feeling sick to your stomach or throwing up; your bladder symptoms not improving after 1-2 days of antibiotics, or getting worse; blood in your urine. You do not need all of these - fever on its own, or back or side pain on its own, is enough of a reason to call. If you cannot reach us, go to urgent care or the emergency room; do not wait for treatment. Always say that you are pregnant and how many weeks. IMPLEMENTER NOTE: this text is authored from ACOG Clinical Consensus No. 4 and ACOG patient FAQ050. It is NOT derived from the ACOG/AIM Urgent Maternal Warning Signs card, which is licensed for distribution only in its entirety and without modification. That card may be linked whole.

Most symptoms go away in 1 to 2 days. It is very important to finish the medication prescribed for a urinary tract infection, even after your symptoms go away - because each untreated infection risks moving up to the kidneys. NOTE: no guideline source addresses what to do about a specific missed dose; that is pharmacy labelling advice and must not be attributed to ACOG. The claim that stopping early causes antibiotic resistance is also not supported by these sources - the sourced reason to finish the course is progression to pyelonephritis.

properties.topic: What we are not recommending, and why
properties.instructions: Cranberry products, probiotics, D-mannose, extra hydration, voiding after intercourse and front-to-back wiping are NOT recommended for preventing urinary infections in pregnancy. This is not an oversight: the one US guideline that covers them explicitly excludes pregnant women, and its evidence review excluded them from study selection. For non-pregnant women, post-coital voiding and wiping direction are described as myths, and a large trial found D-mannose no better than placebo. Front-to-back wiping remains a urine SPECIMEN COLLECTION instruction, which is a different thing. The only prevention measure with a basis in pregnancy is antibiotic suppression, and only after a recurrence.

properties.topic: What group B strep in your urine means
properties.instructions: Your urine test grew a bacterium called group B strep. Two things follow, and both are good to know now. First, you will be given antibiotics through a drip during labour to protect your baby - this happens regardless of the amount grown. Second, you will NOT need the usual group B strep swab at 36-37 weeks, because this result already tells us what that swab would. If the amount grown was high, or you have symptoms, you will also be treated now.

properties.name: Asymptomatic bacteriuria screening completion
properties.measure: Of pregnant patients, the proportion with at least one urine CULTURE (not dipstick) resulted during pregnancy, ideally at or before the first-trimester visit. Steward: local - no national measure exists for prenatal asymptomatic bacteriuria screening, UTI treatment in pregnancy, or outpatient antibiotic stewardship covering urinary infection.
